About us

The City Rail Link is the largest infrastructure project ever to be undertaken in New Zealand. The CRL is a 3.45km twin-tunnel underground rail link up to 42 metres below the city centre transforming the downtown Britomart Transport Centre into a two-way through-station that better connects the Auckland rail network. Auckland’s annual population growth demands the completion of this complex project within tight timeframes. The CRL team are consistently challenged with tunnelling through an established city; construction on reclaimed land; the gradient of the tunnel; and the proximity of our central Britomart station to the harbour. We are proud to say we have a Safety and Sustainability lens on all of our construction work and have embraced Maori design throughout our station design. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GZ_sVPhrB7o

    How do you build New Zealand’s biggest transport infrastructure project? We’re taking you behind the scenes of the incredible story of the City Rail Link in a special five-part video series. Episode two features the engineering giant that made it all possible – our tunnel boring machine. Longer than a rugby field, weighing 910 tonnes, with a 7.15-metre diameter, and capable of housing 12 people inside, this engineering marvel excavated Auckland beneath the city streets. Along the way it helped install the concrete tunnel lining and remove thousands of tonnes of spoil, using more than 64,200 cubic metres of concrete – enough to fill 25 Olympic-sized swimming pools. Take a look back at the machine that carved the path for Auckland’s rail future and the spectacular tunnel breakthroughs.     A dream more than 100 years in the making. An underground railway beneath the heart of Auckland. The idea was first proposed in the 1920s. It was debated, delayed, rejected and almost abandoned more than once. Now it’s real. In Episode 1 of our five-part series on the history of Auckland’s City Rail Link, we look back at the vision that refused to die and the extraordinary engineering challenges that brought it to life — including the remarkable feat of lifting a historic downtown building to make way for New Zealand’s biggest transport infrastructure project.     Tangata whenua Ngāti Whātua Ōrākei led a moving Mahi Ōkawa (formal blessing) across all three new City Rail Link stations today, together with representatives from the eight iwi of the City Rail Link Mana Whenua Forum. The ceremony recognised the cultural and regional significance of Aotearoa New Zealand’s largest transport infrastructure project. It reflected on the strength of the ongoing partnership between mana whenua and City Rail Link project partners, marking an important step as the project enters its final readiness phase. 🚆 A new chapter for Auckland is almost here.     A significant achievement as we move towards completion of New Zealand’s largest transport infrastructure project. City Rail Link has won the Site Safe-sponsored award for Best Governance-Level Engagement in Health & Safety at the 2026 New Zealand Workplace Health & Safety Awards. We are honoured to have been recognised alongside fellow finalists Government Health & Safety Lead and NZ Transport Agency Waka Kotahi. The award was accepted on behalf of CRL by Russell McMullan, CRL Ltd General Manager Assurance and Integration, at last night’s awards ceremony. CRL Chief Executive Patrick Brockie said: “We are very proud of our governance approach to health and safety on the City Rail Link project, including our highly regarded safety stage-gate process, which has played a critical role in supporting safe outcomes throughout delivery.” Organised by Thomson Reuters, publisher of Safeguard magazine, and proudly supported by WorkSafe New Zealand and ACC, the awards recognise excellence in workplace health, safety and wellbeing across New Zealand. From day one, City Rail Link Ltd and Link Alliance set out to achieve industry-leading standards in health, safety and wellbeing. This award reflects the commitment, leadership and dedication of everyone involved in delivering the project safely. Congratulations and thank you to all who have contributed to this outstanding result. #HealthAndSafety #Governance #CityRailLink #RiskManagement
